main_text.p: Eunuchi & mulieres, eo morbo tentarentur, sed etiam caprarum ouium, q; gregem ita infe-stârit, ut vix tertia earum pars extaret libera.

Diofcor.An vero hoc ita euenerit, quia more podagram & Aui-cenna moraarcent, in controuersiam venire potest. Testatur Galenus atq; Hippocr. mora qua fatis maturue-runt, ventrem subducere, stomachumq; squalli-dum astuantem, confolari, preferim frigida si-sint, & paulo ante alios cibos sumantur, moxq; fiat deambulatio, unde Horatius non immerite dixerit, cecinit, Ille salubres, κακοσ- μαχαÆstates peraget, qui nigris prandia mo-ris. Finiet, ante grauem quæ legerit arbore solem.

κα ταPeculiari verò facultate podagricis auxilia-ri, quæ minus illi infestentur, ànemine adhuc vi-di obferuatum. Experimenti via facilis est. Ve-risimile tamen est, ac fieri potuisse credibile mo-ra frequenter Pytharini etate ab omnib. essitat stomachis recreatis aliud, liquatis & emollitę eorum humorum lapsum & prouentum, qui si articulos decumbentes podagram gignere con-sueuerunt, intercipere. Id quod & Galenus con-firmat, dicens, aliquos habentes affectus podagriæ effe obnoxios. Verum de capris & oribus, quæ mororum fructus non attingunt, & tamen ab eâ luce immunes nō extiterunt, quid sentiam, nō oc-currit, nisi quod ex aere inclementia quadam-moris.

page.notes: The left margin notes are small, partly Greek and partly abbreviated; the Greek marginal words (κακοσ-, μαχα, κα τα) are doubtful and are uncertain readings. The ordering of the margin notes beside the text is approximate. Several words in the text have low legibility where the scan is faint, notably in the lines beginning "Finiet" and "Peculiari", and in the Greek line. Some of the printed text near the left edge is damaged; the reading of "Æstates" and "Pytharini" should be checked against the scan.
